releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fixes

- **Resource sync**: Fixed blob path mismatch where `uploadResource` stored blobs at `.resource/<blobId>` but `downloadResource` fetched `.resource/<metaId>`, causing 100% pull failure for non-md files. Now both use the same `metaId`.
- **Force push**: Resources now force-reupload on forcePush (not skip based on stale mapping hash), ensuring old incorrectly-pathed blobs are replaced.
- **Status bar**: Completion status now persists — green `setOk` on success, red `setError` on failure. No more `setIdle()` clearing the result.
- **trimSlash**: Also strips trailing backtick from server URLs.
releases.name: v0.3.53 - Resource blob path fix + status bar persistence

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

**Pull was broken** because `belongsToRoot` rejected items whose parent (`3acbfff...` — the old root folder from a previous version) wasn't in the mapping. With no root folder configured, we should accept everything — the delta cursor already prevents stale data from being pulled.

Also rewrote `InitialSync` to create folder hierarchy on the server (`createFolders`) before uploading notes, fixing first-time sync.
releases.name: v0.3.35

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

**Joplin Server delta API field mismatch.** The delta endpoint returns `item_name` (not `name`). The `as unknown as Paginated<DeltaItem>` cast doesn't transform fields at runtime — `d.name` was `undefined`, causing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')`.

Normalizes in `delta()`: maps `item_name` → `name`, `jop_updated_time` → `updated_time`, and ensures `type` is a number.
releases.name: v0.3.34

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fixes

- **delta cursor after forcePush**: consumes delta stream to set cursor, prevents InitialSync from pulling stale items (2422+ old server artifacts)
- **belongsToRoot with empty rootId**: accepts items with empty parent_id (Joplin root level) or whose parent is in the mapping; rejects stale/foreign items with unknown parent
- **Server check**: 1547 notes, 0 folders exist on server (old broken versions created notes only). ForcePush builds folder structure.

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Change

Removed the `Obsidian` root wrapper folder. All vault directories now sync directly to Joplin root:

```
Before:  Obsidian/ > 2025 AESC/ > 900 GLHRIS/ > 笔记.md
After:   2025 AESC/ > 900 GLHRIS/ > 笔记.md
```

Top-level notes use `parent_id=''` (Joplin root level). Folder hierarchy mirrors vault structure exactly.

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

`getItem` and `getItemBinary` now use `rawRequest` instead of `exec`. The `/content` endpoint returns raw note content (Joplin serialized format), not JSON — no reason to attempt JSON parsing.
releases.name: v0.3.31

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

`putItem` now uses `exec` (JSON path). With `?force=1`, Joplin Server returns JSON — `{"id":...,"updated_time":...,"name":...}`. The previous version tried to parse the response as Joplin serialized format, which failed on JSON responses.
releases.name: v0.3.30

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

**Root cause identified**: Joplin Server `PUT /api/items/root:/:name:/content` returns the **Joplin serialized item** (not JSON). The response body is in Joplin's key:value format with the item content.

Previous code tried `JSON.parse()` on this response, which threw `SyntaxError` for every single note upload — explaining why 0 notes ever appeared on the server.

### What changed
- `putItem` now uses `rawRequest` (no JSON parse) instead of `exec`
- Parses response text as Joplin serialized format (scans last lines for `id:` and `updated_time:`)
- All other API methods (listChildren, delta, etc.) continue to use JSON parsing (they call different endpoints)
releases.name: v0.3.29

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fix

Safe JSON parsing in HTTP response handling. The previous code crashed with `SyntaxError` when Joplin Server returned a non-JSON response body for `PUT /api/items/root:/.../content`.

- **diagnose**: logs status + first 200 chars of response body when JSON parsing fails (first 5 occurrences)
- **safe**: `putItem` throws `ApiError` with the full response snippet instead of a bare `SyntaxError`

Uploads were all failing because the response body couldn't be parsed as JSON. This version logs the ACTUAL response so we can see what the server is returning.
releases.name: v0.3.28

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
## Fixes
- Write-then-verify is now **non-fatal**: logs SHA-256 mismatch, continues instead of throwing
- Adds `?force=1` query param to putItem API calls — forces server to accept overwrites
- Logs **all** upload failures to console (was limited to first 3)
- Folder creation also uses force=true

### If push still fails
Check Obsidian console (Ctrl+Shift+I) for `[joplin-sync]` error messages and report back.

releases.author: yanqingwang
releases.description:
Bidirectional sync, attachments, links, locks.

## Phase 2 — Bidirectional Incremental Sync
- VaultWatcher (file create/modify/delete/rename events)
- ChangeQueue (debounced, persisted, crash-safe)
- LocalPusher (local→remote with folder hierarchy)
- DeltaPuller (remote→local via delta API)
- ConflictResolver (duplicate/local-wins/remote-wins)
- InitialSync (three-way merge)
- SyncEngine state machine (Pushing→Pulling→Resolving)

## Phase 3 — Attachments & Links
- ResourceManager (upload/download resources)
- LinkTransformer (wiki-link↔:joplinId conversion)

## Phase 4 — Robustness
- LockManager (sync lock acquire/refresh/release)
- EncryptionService (E2EE skeleton)

## Remaining
- Full E2EE implementation (Phase 4)
- getSettingDefinitions for Obsidian 1.13+
- LinkTransformer integration into push/pull pipelines
releases.name: v0.2.0 — Phase 2-4
